questions.question: A person in a four-rakah Fard salah realizes they have stood into a fifth rakah, but have not yet completed its Sajdah. What should they do?
options: Remain standing and complete the fifth rakah normally
Return to sitting immediately, complete the Tashahud, and perform سَجْدَةُ السَّهْو
Complete the Sajdah and then perform Sajda Sahu at the end
Break the prayer and restart it from the beginning
questions.explanation: If caught before completing the Sajdah of the fifth rakah, sitting down preserves the Fard prayer; Sajda Sahu is then performed to cover the error.

questions.question: A person has already completed the Sajdah of the fifth rakah. What is the ruling on their Fard prayer?
options: The Fard prayer converts to Nafil and Tasleem is given immediately
The Fard prayer is invalidated and must be restarted
The Fard prayer remains valid with five rakahs
The Fard prayer converts to Nafil (تَحَوَّلَتْ صَلَاتُهُ نَفْلًا) and a sixth rakah must be added
questions.explanation: Once the Sajdah of the fifth rakah is completed the Fard is irrecoverably converted to Nafil; because Nafil cannot validly consist of an odd number of rakahs, a sixth must be added.

questions.question: A person doubts their rakah count for the very first time during a salah. What is required of them?
options: Add an extra rakah as a precaution
Break the prayer and restart it from the beginning
Perform Sajda Sahu only, without restarting
Act on غَالِبُ الظَّنّ and perform Sajda Sahu at the end
questions.explanation: A first-time doubt about the rakah count is serious enough that the salah must be broken and restarted; the rule of acting on غَالِبُ الظَّنّ applies only when the doubt is habitual.

questions.question: A person habitually experiences doubt about their rakah count. How should they handle this doubt?
options: Perform an extra rakah each time they are unsure
Break the prayer and restart it every time the doubt arises
Ignore the doubt entirely and complete the prayer without any compensation
Act on غَالِبُ الظَّنّ and perform Sajda Sahu at the end of the prayer
questions.explanation: For habitual doubt, the worshipper acts on their dominant thought (غَالِبُ الظَّنّ) and then compensates with Sajda Sahu at the end, rather than breaking and restarting.

questions.question: What is the correct progressive hierarchy of positions for Salatul Mareed (prayer for a sick person)?
options: Standing → sitting → laying on one's side (facing Qibla) → إِشَارَة with the head
Standing → laying on one's side → sitting → إِشَارَة
Sitting → standing → laying on one's side → إِشَارَة
إِشَارَة → sitting → standing → laying on one's side
questions.explanation: The sick person begins with standing and moves down the hierarchy only as their condition prevents the higher position; laying on the side facing the Qibla is preferred when lying down is required.

questions.question: A sick person begins their salah using إِشَارَة but recovers mid-salah and is now able to stand. What must they do?
options: Continue the salah from the current point, now standing
Perform Sajda Sahu to compensate for the portion prayed with إِشَارَة
Switch to sitting rather than standing so as not to disrupt the salah
Restart the salah from the beginning (اسْتِئْنَاف الصَّلَاة)
questions.explanation: Recovering to a higher (stronger) position mid-salah requires restarting the prayer; by contrast, deteriorating to a lower position mid-salah is always permitted without restarting.

questions.question: What is the meaning of غَالِبُ الظَّنّ?
options: Head-gesture indication replacing Ruku and Sujood
Restarting the prayer from the beginning
The final sitting position before Tasleem
Dominant or preponderant thought
questions.explanation: غَالِبُ الظَّنّ literally means the dominant or preponderant opinion/thought, and is used in Fiqh to describe acting on one's stronger belief when certainty is unavailable.

questions.question: Which term describes the head-gesture that replaces Ruku and Sujood for a sick person unable to move otherwise?
options: إِشَارَة
تَحَوَّلَتْ صَلَاتُهُ نَفْلًا
اسْتِئْنَاف الصَّلَاة
الْقَعْدَةُ الْأَخِيرَة
questions.explanation: إِشَارَة refers to the head gesture used in Salatul Mareed as the final concession when a sick person cannot physically perform Ruku or Sujood.

questions.question: What does الْقَعْدَةُ الْأَخِيرَة refer to?
options: Restarting the prayer from the beginning
The final sitting position performed before Tasleem
The head-gesture indication used by a sick worshipper
The dominant thought used to resolve doubt about rakah count
questions.explanation: الْقَعْدَةُ الْأَخِيرَة (Qadatul Akhira) is the final sitting in salah, during which the complete Tashahud is recited before Tasleem.

questions.question: What is the meaning of اسْتِئْنَاف الصَّلَاة?
options: The conversion of a Fard prayer into a Nafil prayer
Performing Sajda Sahu after a mistake
Restarting the prayer from the beginning
The final sitting position before Tasleem
questions.explanation: اسْتِئْنَاف الصَّلَاة means to restart the prayer entirely from the beginning, which is required when a sick person recovers to a higher position mid-salah.
